analysis.title: "Worrying Themes At The Edges": Deutsche Maps Every Bond In America And Finds Where AI Credit Is Cracking
key_insights: Deutsche Bank's Research Institute plotted yield against maturity for every bond in the USD investment-grade and high-yield indices and flagged the AI-linked names. Its finding is that AI-linked financing costs are not excessive relative to the rest of the credit stack for now, though the gap widens further out the curve.
AA-rated AI names (Meta, Alphabet, Nvidia, Amazon) sit at or below the bottom of the IG group, borrowing at around 5-5.5% at the front end.
BBB-rated AI names (Oracle and SpaceX) cluster at around 8-8.5% at 10-12 years' duration. That is the top of the IG distribution, roughly 1.5-2pp above most similar-duration bonds.
AI names in high yield are mostly BB rated and sit in the middle of the pack at 7-11%. The widest bonds in the HY index, at 15-19%, are not AI-linked, with the exception of CoreWeave.

CoreWeave (rated BB+) has the top four dots in the widest-HY group. Its unsecured 2032 bonds, sold four months ago, trade below 80 cents on the dollar, a level conventionally seen as distressed, and its five-year CDS closed at 1,118bps on Wednesday.

CoreWeave's bull case per DB: it rents compute on four-to-six year take-or-pay contracts, with a backlog over $100bn, about two-thirds with IG-rated counterparties such as Microsoft, Meta, IBM and Caterpillar. The bond market is reacting more to leverage than to counterparty quality.

DB warns the concern can become a self-fulfilling prophecy and risks triggering broader issues in other AI-related names. It names Oracle as the bellwether: five-year CDS rose 36bp over two days to 288bps. A downgrade from BBB would risk forced sales by IG-only investors.

Duration mismatch: advanced GPUs depreciate over roughly four to six years, in line with contract lengths, but the financing runs longer. DB says the term premium grows with duration, which is why the AI-versus-rest gap widens further out the curve.

Borrowing is accelerating as capex overtakes operating cash flow. Meta needs to fund its planned 5GW Hyperion supercluster in Louisiana at a cost of some $50bn. Broadcom has started lending to AI labs, and private credit and off-balance-sheet data-centre vehicles are growing.
DB's conclusion: as the capex cycle shifts to debt funding, credit price action deserves more respect. AI financing costs are not dramatic overall, but there are worrying themes at the edges.
ZeroHedge commentary (not DB): Gartner predicted over 80% of neoclouds will cease independent operations by 2030, and the article cites a Kospi crash and neocloud liquidations on Oct 14.

sector_views.rationale: Financing costs are not yet excessive, but stress is concentrated at the edges (CoreWeave, Oracle) and the gap widens at longer maturities as capex outpaces cash flow.

vol_and_positioning: Oracle CDS of 288bps and CoreWeave CDS of 1,118bps are the stress gauges DB and the article watch. A BBB downgrade at Oracle would force IG-only holders to sell.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-linked financing costs are not excessive relative to the rest of credit. AA names borrow at 5-5.5%, AI names in HY sit mid-pack at 7-11%, and CoreWeave has a backlog over $100bn, about two-thirds with IG-rated counterparties.
tension_points.bear_case: The gap widens further out the curve, and CoreWeave's CDS at 1,118bps and bonds below 80 cents show stress at the edges. Oracle's CDS rose 36bp in two days, and the concern could become self-fulfilling and spread to other AI names.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An Oracle downgrade from BBB, which would risk forced sales by IG-only investors.
